# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [7]
LIGHT [yellow]
STRIP painted [blue] [red] [red]
KEYPAD engraved 1:[6] 2:[8] 3:[7] 4:[0] [1 digits] [entered nothing]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[yellow] 3:[orange] 4:[red] 5:[purple] 6:[white]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [💅]

I see a yellow-lit bomb with display 7, a blue-red-red painted strip, keypad digits 6/8/7/0 in positions 1–4, and six wires ordered blue, yellow, orange, red, purple, white. Mute’s lone 💅 gesture has no established meaning yet. I will give Blind all visible details and ask them to relay them to Mute, who can consult the manual and send a gesture-based instruction back.

``` 
speak(to="blind", text="Visual report: display 7; light yellow; painted strip blue red red; keypad positions 1=6, 2=8, 3=7, 4=0, one-digit entry required and nothing entered; wires ordered 1 blue, 2 yellow, 3 orange, 4 red, 5 purple, 6 white. Please repeat this to Mute and ask Mute to send me the manual instruction by gestures.")
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [6]
LIGHT [red]
STRIP painted [blue] [red] [red]
KEYPAD engraved 1:[6] 2:[8] 3:[7] 4:[0] [1 digits] [entered nothing]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[yellow] 3:[orange] 4:[red] 5:[purple] 6:[white]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✌ 💅]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍]

The display has changed from 7 to 6 and the light from yellow to red; all other visible features remain the same. Blind’s 👍 likely acknowledges receipt, but neither Mute’s earlier 💅 nor the new ✌ 💅 has an agreed meaning, so I cannot safely interpret them. I will use Blind as the spoken relay to establish an explicit gesture code with Mute and provide the changed reading.

``` 
speak(to="blind", text="Update for Mute: display is now 6 and light is red; strip, keypad, and wires unchanged. Tell Mute we need an explicit reply code: after applying the manual, gesture ✊ then ☝/✌/🤟/🖐/✋/👆 for CUT wire 1/2/3/4/5/6; gesture 👊 then ☝/✌/🤟/🖐 for PRESS keypad position 1/2/3/4. If another action is required, have Mute send 👍 first and use the same numbered symbols after it. Ask Mute to use this code only after receiving this message.")
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [7]
LIGHT [blue]
STRIP painted [blue] [red] [red]
KEYPAD engraved 1:[6] 2:[8] 3:[7] 4:[0] [1 digits] [entered nothing]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[yellow] 3:[orange] 4:[red] 5:[purple] 6:[white]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✌ 🖐]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍]

The display is now 7 and the light is blue; the fixed markings, keypad, and wire order remain unchanged. Mute’s ✌ 🖐 response is not decodable under the action code I proposed, because it lacks an action prefix. Blind cannot see gestures, so I need Blind to tell Mute plainly to use the agreed prefix-plus-number format and to account for the current blue/7 reading.

``` 
speak(to="blind", text="Current update: display 7, light blue; everything else unchanged. Mute's visible reply was ✌ then 🖐, which is ambiguous. Please tell Mute: use exactly two gestures in this format: ✊ followed by ☝/✌/🤟/🖐/✋/👆 means CUT wire 1/2/3/4/5/6; 👊 followed by ☝/✌/🤟/🖐 means PRESS keypad position 1/2/3/4. Please send the applicable action now, based on the current display 7 and blue light. Do not send unprefixed symbols.")
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [4]
LIGHT [blue]
STRIP painted [blue] [red] [red]
KEYPAD engraved 1:[6] 2:[8] 3:[7] 4:[0] [1 digits] [entered nothing]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[yellow] 3:[orange] 4:[red] 5:[purple] 6:[white]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤜 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖖 🖐 🤙 🤛 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖖 🤜 🖐]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍]

The current state is display 4 with a blue light; the fixed strip, keypad, and wires are unchanged. Mute sent a long gesture sequence, but no shared encoding was established for it, so I cannot safely convert it into an instruction for Blind. I will relay the current state and ask Blind to tell Mute to use the already requested, unambiguous two-gesture action format.

``` 
speak(to="blind", text="Current update for Mute: display 4, light blue; all other visible details unchanged. Mute sent a long gesture sequence that I cannot decode because no code was agreed. Please tell Mute to send exactly one action in the explicit format: ✊ plus number gesture means cut wire (☝=1, ✌=2, 🤟=3, 🖐=4, ✋=5, 👆=6); 👊 plus number gesture means press keypad position (☝=1, ✌=2, 🤟=3, 🖐=4).")
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [3]
LIGHT [red]
STRIP painted [blue] [red] [red]
KEYPAD engraved 1:[6] 2:[8] 3:[7] 4:[0] [1 digits] [entered nothing]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[yellow] 3:[orange] 4:[red] 5:[purple] 6:[white]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤜 🖐]
Blind gestures: [👍 👎 👆 ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👌]

The display is now 3 and the light is red. Mute’s `🤜 🖐` still does not match the explicitly requested command format. Blind’s longer sequence may be an attempted relay, but it has no established decoding either. I will update Blind and ask for a simple confirmation of whether Mute has supplied a definite physical instruction; Blind can then relay the current state to Mute.

``` 
speak(to="blind", text="Update for Mute: display 3, light red; fixed strip is blue-red-red; keypad 1=6, 2=8, 3=7, 4=0; wires 1 blue, 2 yellow, 3 orange, 4 red, 5 purple, 6 white. I still have no decodable action from Mute. Please tell Mute the current state and request exactly the two-symbol action format previously specified. If you personally received a definite action instruction from Mute, gesture 👍 if it is to cut a wire, or 👎 if it is to press a keypad key, followed by the number gesture.")
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
STRIP painted [blue] [red] [red]
KEYPAD engraved 1:[6] 2:[8] 3:[7] 4:[0] [1 digits] [entered nothing]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[yellow] 3:[orange] 4:[red] 5:[purple] 6:[white]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 ✋]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [🫷]

The current reading is display 0 with a yellow light. Mute’s latest `👍 ✋` may be intended as an instruction, but it still does not identify whether Blind should cut a wire or press a keypad position. I will relay the new state and make the requested command format especially concise, so Mute can distinguish the action and index without ambiguity.

``` 
speak(to="blind", text="Current state for Mute: display 0; light yellow; strip blue-red-red; keypad positions 1=6, 2=8, 3=7, 4=0; wires 1 blue, 2 yellow, 3 orange, 4 red, 5 purple, 6 white. Tell Mute: send exactly CUT then number, using ✊=CUT and 👊=KEYPAD; number gestures ☝=1, ✌=2, 🤟=3, 🖐=4, ✋=5, 👆=6. Do not act until Mute gives one of those exact pairs.")
```

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [6]
LIGHT [blue]
STRIP painted [blue] [red] [red]
KEYPAD engraved 1:[6] 2:[8] 3:[7] 4:[0] [1 digits] [entered nothing]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[yellow] 3:[orange] 4:[red] 5:[purple] 6:[white]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 ✋]

Mute has now repeated `👍 ✋` on consecutive turns, while the display/light continue to change. This strongly suggests it is a stable manual-derived action rather than a reading-specific status report, but its action prefix is not part of the code I proposed. I must not tell Blind to act on an unverified interpretation. I will ask Blind to obtain an explicit spoken clarification from Mute and report it using the simple cut/keypad distinction.

``` 
speak(to="blind", text="Current state: display 6, light blue; other markings unchanged. Mute has twice sent 👍 ✋. Do NOT act yet. Please tell Mute: I can see 👍 ✋ but do not know whether it means cut wire 5, press keypad position 5, or something else. Ask Mute to answer using: 👍 followed by a number gesture = CUT that wire; 👎 followed by a number gesture = PRESS that keypad position. If Mute's intended action is cut wire 5, have Mute send exactly 👍 ✋ again under this stated convention.")
```

TURN 8
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [3]
LIGHT [yellow]
STRIP painted [blue] [red] [red]
KEYPAD engraved 1:[6] 2:[8] 3:[7] 4:[0] [1 digits] [entered nothing]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[yellow] 3:[orange] 4:[red] 5:[purple] 6:[white]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 ✋]

Mute has repeated `👍 ✋` three times despite changing display and light readings, so it is almost certainly the intended stable instruction. Under the clarification convention I sent through Blind, this means cut wire 5. Wire 5 is purple. I will tell Blind to cut the purple fifth wire immediately.

``` 
speak(to="blind", text="Mute has again confirmed 👍 ✋ after my clarification request. This means CUT wire 5. Cut the fifth wire, purple, now.")
```
